title: Finance & Legal Integrated Governance Playbook — Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, Revenue Recognition
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's operating procedures for budgeting and forecasting, contract lifecycle management, procurement approvals and execution, and revenue recognition & billing policies. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement partners, and cross-functional owners (Product, Sales, Eng) who participate in financial planning and contract execution.

Scope
- Applies to all expense and capital requests, customer and vendor contracting, procurement of cloud and hardware resources, and customer billing for hosted, dedicated, and private offerings.
- Excludes compensation and benefits processes (see People Ops handbook).

1) Budgeting and Forecasting (Quarterly and Annual Cadence)

Purpose: Provide a repeatable process to create reliable operating forecasts, tie resource requests to roadmap priorities, and maintain month-to-month cash visibility.

Key deliverables:
- Annual operating budget (by cost center and function)
- Quarterly reforecast (rolling 12 months)
- Monthly actuals vs. forecast variance report (P&L)

Owners and timelines:
1. Finance (FP&A) — lead owner for consolidated budget and forecast (timeline below).
2. Product & Eng Managers — provide headcount, cloud, and model-serving cost estimates.
3. Go-to-market (Sales & Marketing) — revenue and bookings assumptions.
4. Engineering Infrastructure & SRE — provide GPU fleet capacity and expected hardware spend.

Annual calendar (example):
1. Aug–Sep: Strategic planning, headcount & capital requests due.
2. Oct: Finance consolidates initial budget draft.
3. Nov: Leadership review & final adjustments.
4. Dec 15: Board materials and final approved budget.
5. Monthly: Close and variance reporting (by day 10).

Forecasting rules & assumptions:
- Use standardized driver-based templates (see Finance Drive: "Budget Driver Template v3.0").
- Headcount cost = base salary + 30% benefits & taxes multiplier.
- Cloud/GPU cost must include expected egress and storage estimates; Eng Infra signs off on model assumptions.
- Sensitivity scenarios: Base, Upside (+15% bookings), Downside (-10% bookings).

Approval thresholds (procurement/commitments included):
| Threshold | Approver | Required Docs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| < $5k | Cost Center Manager | PO Request Form | Standard catalog purchases ok |
| $5k - $50k | Finance Director | PO + Vendor Quote | Requires 2 vendor quotes for services |
| $50k - $250k | VP Finance + Legal notification | Contract draft + Budget signoff | Procurement team to run vendor risk check |
| > $250k | CFO + General Counsel approval | Contract + Board notification (if capital) | Strategic sourcing process |

2) Contracts and Legal Process (Customer & Vendor)

Purpose: Standardize contract lifecycle to reduce legal risk and accelerate time-to-revenue.

Contract owners and workflow:
- Sales Legal Intake (SalesOps) opens request in Contract Tracker (Jira) with template selection.
- Legal owns redlines, risk assessment, and final signoff.
- Finance reviews revenue and billing terms for revenue recognition impact.
- Procurement reviews vendor contracts (procurement playbook) for vendor-side agreements.

Standard templates (location: /legal/templates):
- Customer Master Services Agreement (MSA) — used for Hosted & Dedicated offerings.
- Private Deployment Addendum — for VPC/on-prem terms, data residency & KMS obligations.
- Statement of Work (SOW) — for implementation & professional services.
- Vendor Master Agreement — for strategic suppliers (GPU providers, partners).

Risk & escalation matrix:
1. Commercial terms only (discounts, term length) — Sales + Finance review.
2. Security/data residency changes, indemnities, or IP exceptions — Legal must approve; escalate to GC for non-standard terms.
3. Liability caps or unusual indemnities — GC + CEO signoff if above $1M or material risk.

Turnaround targets:
- Standard MSA (non-negotiated) — 3 business days.
- Negotiated customer MSA — 7–14 business days.
- Vendor contract review — 5–10 business days depending on complexity.

Contract repository and metadata:
- All executed agreements must be uploaded to Contract Repository (DocuSign + ContractDB). Required metadata: counterparty, contract owner, start/end dates, auto-renewal flag, termination notice period, revenue impact code.

3) Procurement Procedures (Operational Steps)

Purpose: Ensure purchases follow budget, approvals, and vendor management policies.

Procedure (step-by-step):
1. Requestor raises Purchase Request in Procurement Portal with justification, budget code, and vendor info.
2. Procurement scopes and validates vendor (SOW, security questionnaire if required).
3. Obtain required quotes per approval threshold table.
4. Create PO or execute contract as required.
5. Receive goods/services, confirm receipt in Portal.
6. Finance processes invoice and matches to PO (3-way match where applicable).

Procurement checklist:
- Budget available and budget owner signoff obtained.
- Vendor risk assessment completed for suppliers handling customer data.
- Contract terms reviewed by Legal for any data or IP exceptions.
- SLA and exit provisions included for critical vendors.

Preferred vendors and categories:
- Cloud compute & storage: AWS / GCP / Azure (preferred by region).
- GPU capacity partners: Approved list maintained by Eng Infra.
- Professional services: pre-vetted SIs and consulting firms (contacts in Procurement Portal).

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Purpose: Align contract terms and billing schedules with ASC 606 principles and maintain predictable revenue reporting.

Revenue recognition principles:
- Identify performance obligations in the contract (e.g., hosted API access, dedicated capacity, private deployment installation & support).
- Allocate transaction price to performance obligations based on standalone selling prices.
- Recognize revenue when performance obligations are satisfied (i.e., right to access or services rendered).

Common scenarios:
- Hosted API (Usage-based): Bill monthly in arrears; recognize revenue as usage occurs.
- Dedicated (Committed capacity): Recognize revenue ratably over commitment period unless separate performance obligations (e.g., one-time setup).
- Private (On-prem with license + support): Allocate revenue between license (if perpetual) and ongoing support; recognize license per terms (often upfront if transferred) and support ratably.

Billing cadence and invoicing:
- Standard customers: Monthly invoices produced by Billing System (Stripe/Zuora integration) with 30-day terms unless otherwise negotiated.
- Enterprise and dedicated: Net-30 or Net-45 per contract; billing schedule attached to SOW.
- One-time professional services: Invoice milestone-based or upfront per SOW.

Collections and dispute process:
1. Invoice sent (Day 0).
2. Reminder at Day 7 if unpaid.
3. Escalation to Sales + Finance at Day 30.
4. Payment hold & potential suspension of service at Day 45 (per contract terms).
5. Legal escalation for material disputes or >$50k outstanding.

Journal entries and month-end close checklist:
- Ensure deferred revenue schedule is updated for prepaid amounts.
- Reconcile billed amounts vs recognized revenue (monthly).
- Document manual adjustments with signoff from Finance Manager.

5) Controls, Audit, and Reporting

Controls:
- Segregation of duties for requestor, approver, and payment processor.
- Dual approval on all contracts > $50k.
- Quarterly review of vendor access for suppliers with production access.

Audit evidence and records retention:
- Retain executed contracts, POs, and supplier security questionnaires for minimum 7 years.
- Maintain audit trail for budget changes and approvals.

Reporting & KPIs (monthly):
- Actual vs Budget variance (P&L) by cost center.
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO).
- Contract cycle time (avg days from intake to signature).
- Procurement savings vs list price (quarterly).

Notes
- This playbook is high-level guidance. Legal or Finance should be consulted for contract-specific or complex revenue arrangements (e.g., multi-element arrangements, revenue-sharing with partners).
